Dynamics API

Player Specification

See PlayerSpec for the full constructor reference.

DifferentialGamesBase.PlayerSpec — Type
PlayerSpec{T}

Specification for a single player in a PD-GNEP.

Fields

  • id::Int : Player identifier
  • n::Int : State dimension
  • m::Int : Control dimension
  • x0::Vector{T} : Initial state
  • dynamics::Function : Dynamics function fᵢ(xᵢ, uᵢ, p, t)
  • objective::PlayerObjective : Cost functional
  • constraints::Vector{PrivateConstraint} : Player-specific constraints
  • info::AbstractInformationStructure : What this player observes; defaults to PerfectStateInformation(). Used by DifferentialGame to pick the resulting AbstractGameProblem subtype (see _infer_game_class).

Notes

Used to build PD-GNEPs where each player has separable dynamics. Defined before GNEP.jl so that PDGNEProblem can reference PlayerSpec.

ForwardDiff Compatibility

Nonlinear solvers (iLQGames, ALGAMES) differentiate dynamics using ForwardDiff.jl. Dynamics functions must be compatible:

  • Use generic arithmetic (+, *, etc.) rather than type-specific operations.
  • Avoid Float64-typed allocations inside the dynamics; let Julia infer the element type.
  • Do not use branches that depend on values — use smooth approximations instead.
# Good — ForwardDiff compatible
dyn = (x, u, p, t) -> [x[2]; u[1] - 0.1 * x[2]]

# Bad — Float64 literal breaks dual number propagation
dyn = (x, u, p, t) -> [x[2]; Float64(u[1])]
